title: Algorithmic Frontier for Actual Causation via Structural Simplification with Explicit Local Tables
banked_reason: Cold-tier verdict: tier=subfield; target/floor=field; paper_score_ceiling=7.2 < ceiling_for_field=7.4; salvageable=false; improvement_directive=null; ceiling_directive=null.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved exact minimum-cost optimization and replayable certificates when the relevant full-graph component has cycle rank at most one, together with NP-completeness for deterministic binary endogenous chains coupled by shared exogenous roots. Citation re-audit verified the bounded-clause SAT source, and the final math receipt passed; the package nevertheless missed the field floor because it did not connect the two regimes with a matching cycle-rank-two (or other fixed-rank-above-one) hardness construction. A future re-raise should reuse the proved rank-≤1 and chain gadgets and target that missing boundary.
tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but the definition itself gives no exact algorithmic frontier. Under finite explicit local tables, the project proves a relevant-component frontier: the answer is immediately negative when \(X\) and \(Y\) lie in different weak full-graph components; otherwise arbitrary unrelated components are harmless, and an exact certificate calculus is polynomial whenever their common component has cycle rank at most one. A rank-zero component first yields a directed-reachability cut when \(X\) cannot reach \(Y\), and only a reachable instance invokes the linear-arithmetic value-path compiler; a rank-one component uses the exceptional-edge min-sum program. The backend returns a witness and exact optimum certificate or a separating cut. A shared-selector construction separately proves NP-completeness even for deterministic binary models whose endogenous graph is one directed chain, showing why the positive full-graph restriction is substantive.
gap: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual supplies a same-signature structural-simplification representative but no compiler, certificate system, minimum-cost result, or complexity classification. Existing causal-tree algorithms and SAT encodings concern Halpern--Pearl causation and do not enforce Beckers's full-graph reachability legality or actual-row freezing.
fill: The project proves an extensional compiler theorem, an exact additive optimum formula with independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates, and a restricted NP-completeness theorem. The parameterized shared-selector obstruction shows precisely why two deletion histories with the same endogenous value state can differ in full-graph legality.
